campaign_name: Florida Decides Healthcare – Medicaid Expansion (Provide Medicaid Coverage to Eligible Low-Income Adults, Initiative 18-16) – 2028 cycle
purpose: Constitutional amendment to expand Medicaid to adults 18-64 with incomes at or below 138% of the federal poverty level
sponsor: Florida Decides Healthcare (Executive Director Mitch Emerson)
circulation_firm: unknown for 2028. For the 2026 drive, The Outreach Team posted paid 'Petitioner' jobs (posted April 8, 2025).
signatures_required: 880,062 was the 2026-cycle requirement (8% of voters). The exact 2028 figure is unknown.
deadline: Feb 1, 2028 (standard Florida deadline for the 2028 ballot; not separately confirmed in sources)
signatures_collected: Brevard County: 100 valid in total (7 valid 9/1-9/30/2026) as of 9/30/2026. Monroe County: 125 verified as of 1/30/2026. Statewide 2028 total unknown. The 2026 drive validated 75,855 of 90,250 submitted.
pay_rate: 2026 drive (The Outreach Team, April 2025 posting): $19/hr for circulators, $21-25/hr for leadership, +$1/hr bilingual. The 2028 rate is unknown.
hiring_link: https://careers.arena.run/companies/the-outreach-team-2/jobs/48573140-petitioner-help-expand-medicaid-in-florida (2025 posting for the 2026 drive; current status unknown)
evidence_note: Relaunched signature collection for 2028 on Feb 1, 2026. The new model is mail-in petitions (prepaid return envelope) requested through the website, plus 100+ grassroots partners; that model points away from paid field circulation. Brevard's monthly valid count is small (7 in September 2026), which points to low field activity. The group says HB 1205 'dramatically increased petition costs.' It was lead plaintiff in Florida Decides Healthcare v. Byrd. On April 30, 2026, Judge Walker upheld the circulator registration requirement, the out-of-state and non-citizen circulator bans, felon restrictions, the $50,000-per-violation fine and the felony for filling in petition information. Ballot Access News reported the plaintiffs did not plan to appeal (BAN's May 1 post said the ruling would be appealed, so these conflict). The Florida DOS initiative database (constitutionalinitiatives.dos.fl.gov) was blocked by Cloudflare and could not be checked directly.

campaign_name: Smart & Safe Florida – Adult-Use Marijuana (2028 cycle)
purpose: Constitutional amendment legalizing adult personal use of marijuana
sponsor: Smart & Safe Florida (political committee; backed by Trulieve)
signatures_required: Roughly 880,000 (8% of voters), per Cannabis Business Times
deadline: Feb 1, 2028 (standard Florida deadline; not separately confirmed in sources)
signatures_collected: unknown. It must restart collection for 2028.
budget_or_spend: Trulieve contributed $67 million to the 2026 effort. The 2028 budget is unknown.
evidence_note: Cannabis Business Times (Oct 5, 2026) calls Smart & Safe 'active for 2028' and says it must restart the ~880,000-signature collection. No 2028 hiring posts or firm payments were found. The search budget ran out before FL DOE campaign finance could be checked. Because its 2026 drive used a large paid workforce, this is the most likely large paid-circulation buyer in the region for 2027-28, but that is not confirmed.

campaign_name: Smart & Safe Florida – Adult Personal Use of Marijuana (Initiative 25-01) – 2026 cycle
purpose: Constitutional amendment legalizing adult personal use of marijuana for the 2026 ballot
circulation_firm: unknown (the committee cited 474 trained circulators, including out-of-state circulators until May 2, 2025)
signatures_collected: About 1.4 million claimed submitted; 783,592 validated (as of Feb 2, 2026). Failed to qualify.
evidence_note: Paid circulation is confirmed by a headline about a 'paid petitioner working for Florida cannabis campaign' (Ganjapreneur; article body not fetched). HB 1205 impact per the committee's court filing: out-of-state circulators were dropped on May 2, 2025; about 600 Florida-resident circulators stopped because of the 10-day return rule; weekly collection fell about one-third from ~78,000/week; and lawyers estimated $23.7M in potential fines ($50k x 474 circulators). Nearly 71,000 signatures were disqualified, and the AG opened fraud probes. All 22 active initiatives failed to make the 2026 ballot.

purpose: Statewide initiative process (still not restored) and ballot access
signatures_required: Proposed SCR 518 would require 10% of registered voters (~170,000); not in effect. Independent statewide candidate: 1,000 (due Feb 2, 2026).
evidence_note: Mississippi's initiative process has not been confirmed restored. SCR 518 (Sen. Jeremy England) passed the Senate Elections Committee in Feb 2026. It would allow statutory-only initiatives, exclude abortion and PERS, and needs two-thirds of the Senate by Feb 12 plus House action and a statewide vote. Its final 2026 outcome could not be confirmed before the search budget ran out. Even if adopted, it requires voter ratification, so no initiative drive is possible yet.
